src/updater.ts smokeTest scrubs the environment but not the filesystem or uid: the package's server.js runs as the app user and can read DATA_DIR (secret.key, users.json) during the up-to-25 s test. src/release.ts compareVersions returns 0 as soon as two components differ as strings but are numerically equal (1.02.9 vs 1.2.3). It can wrongly refuse a newer package but never accepts an older one; reject leading zeros in VERSION_PATTERN.

local_checks.invariant: a low-trust caller must not be able to fill and rotate away the audit trail (the failed-login path is deduplicated per key and minute for this reason)

local_checks.invariant: forwarded copies and alerts carry no secret, never block the request, and fail closed on a broken secret

Thumbnail tools (pdftoppm, ffmpeg, vips) run as the app uid with no rlimit (memory/CPU) or filesystem sandbox: a memory-safety bug in them could read DATA_DIR/secret.key; the 10 s timeout and 2 slots bound time only. Video and PDF have no pixel/memory gate (only images use maxPixels).

Thumbnail queue (2 running, 16 waiting) is global: an anonymous holder of a public file or share link can keep thumbnails answering 503 for others, and timeouts are not cached as failures, so a slow crafted PDF re-costs 10 s per request. Effect is limited to thumbnails.

Thumbnail cache key is path|size|mtime|size, not content; an owner who rewrites a file keeping size and mtime (WebDAV X-OC-Mtime) leaves viewers a stale picture until the 30 day prune. Same-owner only, not a boundary crossing.
The thumbnail cache of a deleted or purged file stays up to THUMB_CACHE_DAYS but is reachable only through a path that exists with the same size and mtime.
